quiz.question: What do functions do for a big program?

answers.answer: They make the program use less memory automatically
They break it into small, named pieces that each do one job
They make the program colorful and nice to look at
They translate the program into another language

quiz.explanation: Functions split a big program into small, reusable pieces with clear names. Each one does a single job and can be called from anywhere.

quiz.question: What does the principle "don't repeat yourself" mean in programming?

answers.answer: Never use the same variable name twice
Avoid writing the same logic in many places by putting it in one reusable function
Only run the program once to save time
Say every instruction out loud just once

quiz.explanation: "Don't repeat yourself" means you should write a piece of logic once, usually as a function, and reuse it. This keeps your code shorter and easier to maintain.

quiz.question: Why is fixing a bug easier when the logic lives inside a function?

answers.answer: Functions warn you with a sound when something is wrong
You fix it in one place and every call to that function gets the fix
Bugs cannot happen inside a function at all

quiz.explanation: When logic lives in one function, a single fix updates every spot that uses it. Without functions, you would have to find and fix the same bug in many places.
